Three small molecules, each computed with the same input in ORCA and in Gaussian (B3LYP, def2-TZVPP for
water and def2-TZVP for TiCl₄ and the methyl radical; tight SCF). The test set lets you check that both
parsers give the same orbital energies, including the open-shell UKS case. A second step uses two ORCA
r²SCAN-3c optimisations from `files/`.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g01_h2o_pure.out` — ORCA, B3LYP/def2-TZVPP single point, H₂O (closed shell)
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log` — Gaussian 16 twin of the same job
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g04_ticl4.out` — ORCA, B3LYP/def2-TZVP single point, TiCl₄ (Gaussian twin `gaussian/g04_ticl4.log`)
* `tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g03_ch3_uks.out` — ORCA, UKS B3LYP/def2-TZVP, CH₃• doublet (Gaussian twin `gaussian/g03_ch3_uks.log`)
* `files/opt.out` — ORCA, r²SCAN-3c OptTS Freq, Ru complex
* `files/test.out` — ORCA, r²SCAN-3c Opt Freq, C₉H₈NS

**1. ORCA and Gaussian, closed and open shell.** One row per file, in the order given.

```bash
frog-cdft tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g01_h2o_pure.out tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g01_h2o_pure.log tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g04_ticl4.out tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g04_ticl4.log tests/data/gaussian_ref/orca/g03_ch3_uks.out tests/data/gaussian_ref/gaussian/g03_ch3_uks.log
```

```text
ℹ  Parsing g01_h2o_pure.out...
ℹ  Parsing g01_h2o_pure.log...
ℹ  Parsing g04_ticl4.out...
ℹ  Parsing g04_ticl4.log...
ℹ  Parsing g03_ch3_uks.out...
ℹ  Parsing g03_ch3_uks.log...
                            Conceptual DFT (CDFT) Global Indices
╭──────────────────┬───────────┬───────────┬──────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬──────────╮
│ File             │ HOMO (eV) │ LUMO (eV) │ Gap (eV) │ μ (eV) │ η (eV) │ ω (eV) │ S (1/eV) │
├──────────────────┼───────────┼───────────┼──────────┼────────┼────────┼────────┼──────────┤
│ g01_h2o_pure.out │    -8.635 │     0.441 │    9.076 │ -4.097 │  9.076 │  0.925 │    0.110 │
│ g01_h2o_pure.log │    -8.635 │     0.441 │    9.076 │ -4.097 │  9.076 │  0.925 │    0.110 │
│ g04_ticl4.out    │    -9.343 │    -4.011 │    5.332 │ -6.677 │  5.332 │  4.180 │    0.188 │
│ g04_ticl4.log    │    -9.343 │    -4.011 │    5.332 │ -6.677 │  5.332 │  4.180 │    0.188 │
│ g03_ch3_uks.out  │    -6.447 │    -2.069 │    4.378 │ -4.258 │  4.378 │  2.071 │    0.228 │
│ g03_ch3_uks.log  │    -6.447 │    -2.069 │    4.378 │ -4.258 │  4.378 │  2.071 │    0.228 │
╰──────────────────┴───────────┴───────────┴──────────┴────────┴────────┴────────┴──────────╯
```

* Each ORCA/Gaussian pair gives identical numbers, so the two parsers read the same orbital energies.
* Water has the largest gap (η = 9.076 eV) and a positive LUMO (+0.441 eV): it is hard and a poor
  electrophile (ω = 0.925 eV).
* TiCl₄ has the lowest LUMO (−4.011 eV, the empty Ti 3d set; see the `frog-mo` example) and is
  the best electrophile of the three (ω = 4.180 eV). This is the expected order for a Lewis-acidic d⁰ metal
  halide.
* CH₃• is open shell. The HOMO (−6.447 eV) is the singly occupied α orbital and the LUMO (−2.069 eV) is
  the empty β orbital on the same carbon, so the "gap" of 4.378 eV is an α/β difference and not a
  closed-shell HOMO–LUMO gap. Compare radicals only with other radicals.
* The three molecules use two basis sets (def2-TZVPP, def2-TZVP). For a real ranking, use one level
  of theory for the whole series.

**2. Export for a spreadsheet.** `--format csv` prints full precision and `-q` hides the progress
messages. Add `--table-file cdft.csv` to write the table to a file.

```bash
frog-cdft files/opt.out files/test.out --format csv -q
```

```text

File,HOMO (eV),LUMO (eV),Gap (eV),μ (eV),η (eV),ω (eV),S (1/eV)

test.out,-3.99523015140845,-0.7248296954343824,3.270400455974068,-2.360029923421416,3.270400455974068,0.8515381089294741,0.30577295149690054
```

With the same functional (r²SCAN-3c), the Ru complex in `opt.out` is much more electrophilic
(ω ≈ 4.04 eV, η ≈ 2.09 eV) than the organic molecule in `test.out` (ω ≈ 0.85 eV, η ≈ 3.27 eV).
